newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re not planning share buyback.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re not planning share buyback.

text.p: Swiss Re chief executive Walter Kielholz said Swiss Re had a standing policy of holding some stake in its own shares, but it was not planning any new share buybacks.
"Don't write that we are going out to buy a large new amount of shares. That is not the case," Kielholz told a news conference.
Kielholz said that it was standing policy at Swiss Re to buy its own shares from the market.
Earlier on Tuesday Swiss share traders said there was a local news service report stating that Swiss Re disclosed plans to buy back up to 10 percent of its own shares.
But Kielholz said Swiss law limited companies to holding a maximum of 10 percent of their own shares and required them to return the shares to the market within two years or face stiff taxes.
He also said the 1996 annual report showed, for example, how actively Swiss Re bought its own shares on the market.
According to the 1996 report, Swiss Re bought 354,303 of its own registered shares for 443 million Swiss francs last year. That added to an existing holding from 1995 of 791,971 shares.
The total number of registered shares outstanding at the end of 1996 was 15.04 million and of that total the company held 1.03 million. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
